boards.title: Your First Weekend at George Fox University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A conservative, under-21-safe sequence for learning the Newberg campus through dining, recreation, study spaces, history, arts, and student-accessible facilities.

cards.title: Start with a Campus Dinner
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Find the main dining room
cards.notes: Bring your student ID and confirm the posted meal period before meeting classmates in the main dining area overlooking Hess Creek Canyon.
cards.short_summary: Use the first meal to learn the layout of George Fox’s primary dining facility.
cards.evidence_claim: Canyon Commons contains a 900-seat main dining area, smaller meeting spaces, and a cafe; entry during dining hours requires a student ID and meal swipe.
cards.source_title: Meal Plans at George Fox University
cards.access_notes: A student ID and meal swipe are required for dining-hall entry during dining hours; verify the current service schedule before going.

cards.title: Choose a Friday Activity
cards.subtitle: Friday night · Games, courts, track, or climbing
cards.notes: Sign the required liability release, enter through the north glass doors, and ask the welcome desk which recreation areas are available.
cards.short_summary: Turn Friday night into an active introduction to campus recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: Hadlock Student Center includes three sport courts, a fitness center, indoor track, climbing wall, fitness studios, and a rental center.
cards.access_notes: Academic-year Friday hours are listed as 6 a.m.–10 p.m. A liability release is required, and facility access policies apply.

cards.title: Map Out Your Study Options
cards.subtitle: Friday night · Preview the 24-hour space
cards.notes: Use your student ID to enter the 24-hour area, then note the collaborative tables, printers, restrooms, and quieter upstairs carrels.
cards.short_summary: Learn where to work alone or with a group before classes accelerate.
cards.evidence_claim: Murdock Library’s main floor has a 24-hour collaborative study area available to the George Fox community through round-the-clock ID-card access.
cards.access_notes: The 24-hour space requires George Fox ID-card access; other library floors and services follow separate posted hours.

cards.title: Meet at the Center of the Quad
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Establish a campus landmark
cards.notes: Use the 65-foot tower as a meeting point, listen for its daytime quarter-hour chime, and orient yourself to the surrounding quad.
cards.short_summary: Anchor your mental map of campus at its central tower and original bell.
cards.evidence_claim: Centennial Tower stands in the center of the quad, was built in 1991 for the university’s centennial, and contains the original 1891 college bell.
cards.access_notes: View the tower from the quad; the source says its chimes operate during daytime hours and not on Saturday mornings.

cards.title: Read the Oldest Building’s Story
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Campus-history stop
cards.notes: Walk to the quad-side exterior and compare the restored historic building with its official account before continuing across campus.
cards.short_summary: Connect the present campus to its Friends Pacific Academy beginnings.
cards.evidence_claim: Minthorn Hall is George Fox University’s oldest building, predates the university, and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
cards.access_notes: Treat this as an exterior history stop unless the building is officially open; the university has documented renovation during 2025–2026.

cards.title: Find the Mama Bear Statue
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · Alumni Plaza landmark
cards.notes: Pause between Bauman and Stoffer to photograph the 10-foot bronze Mama Bear and learn why the plaza honors university alumni.
cards.short_summary: Use a prominent bronze landmark to connect the arts and athletics sides of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Alumni Plaza sits between Bauman Auditorium and Stoffer Family Stadium and centers on a 10-foot-tall, 800-pound bronze bear called Mama Bear.
cards.access_notes: The source describes an outdoor plaza; remain in designated pedestrian areas and respect any event controls nearby.

cards.title: Locate the Bruins’ Home Field
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Athletics orientation
cards.notes: View the stadium from an authorized public approach, identify Lemmons Family Field, and check athletics listings before planning a game visit.
cards.short_summary: Learn where George Fox football and track-and-field events take place.
cards.evidence_claim: Stoffer Family Stadium is home to George Fox football and track and field and includes a covered grandstand, Lemmons Family Field, and Duke Athletic Center.
cards.access_notes: General facility access is not established by the source; enter only for a scheduled event or when the university permits access.

cards.title: Check the Campus Performance Venue
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Arts and chapel orientation
cards.notes: Find the main entrance, then consult the university calendar or box office before returning for a concert, lecture, chapel, or production.
cards.short_summary: Identify the large auditorium used for music, lectures, chapel, and theatre.
cards.evidence_claim: Bauman Auditorium seats 1,119 and is used for chapel, special lectures, theatrical productions, and band, choir, and orchestra concerts.
cards.access_notes: Interior access depends on scheduled programming and university access controls; check the current event listing before entering.

cards.title: Look for the Current Art Exhibit
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Ross Center gallery stop
cards.notes: Check whether the Ross Center is open, then look for the rotating Lindgren Gallery exhibit without entering restricted rehearsal areas.
cards.short_summary: Add a compact visual-arts stop beside the campus performing-arts facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Donald H. Lindgren Gallery is housed in the Ross Center and hosts rotating exhibits, including student artwork, throughout the year.
cards.access_notes: Gallery access depends on Ross Center opening and exhibit schedules; practice areas have separate eligibility and key-card restrictions.

cards.title: Finish with a Sunday Swim or Workout
cards.subtitle: Sunday · Use the student-access partnership
cards.notes: Show your current George Fox student ID at the front desk, ask which facilities are available, and confirm the day’s pool schedule first.
cards.short_summary: Close the weekend at the public recreation facility beside campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Current George Fox traditional undergraduates and Newberg-based graduate students receive free access to Chehalem Aquatic & Fitness Center by showing a student ID.
cards.access_notes: Show a current George Fox student ID at the center’s front desk. Pool availability may differ from overall facility hours.
